name: TS391LT
notes: The manufacturer's curve at every point the manufacturer states: 90 C at 90 s, 130 C at 180 s, liquidus 138 C at 210 s, peak 165 C at 240 s, back through 138 C at 270 s. Chip Quik call it a starting point for process optimisation, not a finished recipe. Only the opening is this oven's own: the digitised chart asked 1.33 C/s from cold, where measurement gives about 0.58 including the oven's transport lag, and runs 0005 and 0007 both lagged it by 21 s at 45 C and then overtook it by 15 s at 90 C -- a wind-up and an overshoot in the first ninety seconds, worth 23 C of tracking error, all of it before the paste has done anything. The opening now follows the measured rate curve scaled to land exactly on 90 C at 90 s, which the datasheet does specify. THE DOOR MUST BE OPENED AT PEAK: the descent from 165 C to 138 C in 30 s is -0.90 C/s and this oven manages about -0.13 C/s shut. The oven asks for it when opening it will land time above liquidus mid-window, and counts down to it. The datasheet also gives a maximum operating temperature of 96 C after assembly: a board built with this paste must not be baked or held above that afterwards.
reference: Chip Quik TS391LT datasheet rev 1.3, Recommended Profile chart (Sn42/Bi57.6/Ag0.4, mp 138 C); opening ramp generated from data/oven-characterisation.json
